review_resolved: independent review of 8fbd2bc6 (PASS; V1 medium, V2-V4 low); every finding is addressed in f5da300e under Decision 0117, which narrows the Decision 0115 V2 statement and closes the Decision 0116 resumed-run gap

components.review_fixes: a resumed run declares neither recoverability nor context views: the live host service answers both unavailable, the effect recorder refuses a resumed request (declare_run) and the context port marks its views incomplete for a resumed request or composition (V1); the Story 23.4 check allows `requested` in request_tool only as the parameter, one destructuring and requested.origin and refuses any origin assignment in the runtime loop (V2); tests of the live service's declaration gating, the CLI's verification of received declarations, the IPC capacity refusal through a pure answer function, the 64-view bound and the ended accessors (V3); a public line reader over a descriptor reader and an injectable selection prompt, both tested (V4)
components.AMR-04.6.1: kernel/engine/migrations/operational-store/0021-job-control-ledgers.sql (append-only roots and entries, forward-only head); kernel/engine/src/job_ledger_store.rs (DurableJobLedgers: create, observation, control under an owner-supplied client scope, owner-only observe_owner; each append and its head in one immediate transaction naming the head it read; replay on every read; verify_all on open and export; poison on integrity failure); kernel/engine/src/job_control.rs (client-scoped request identities, entry format 2); kernel/engine/src/operational_store.rs (schema 21 after verifying prior history, three content-free export families, DurableAuthorityRuntime::job_ledgers)

mutation_checks: run before the source commit with private tooling, each reverting one rule and running the new tests: ten review-fix mutations each made a new test fail (the resumed-run rule in the live service, the effect recorder and context composition; the 64-view bound; the IPC declaration bound; the CLI run check; the session's terminal and busy gate; the prompt's re-ask; the public reader's overflow policy and its bound). Five AMR-04.6.1 mutations each made a store or ledger test fail (head update outside the append transaction, no canonical encoding check, no replay on open, no poisoning, no client scope). The engine ended-accessor test and the V2 checker were not mutation-run; the V2 unit test is itself a set of source mutants. These runs are not retained logs
failure_comparison: linux 188 passed, 19 failed, 51 ignored and host 345 passed, 52 failed, 10 ignored; both failure name sets are identical to the batch 8 source-check baseline; every new test passes

retained_failures.cause: one intermittent failure of native_inference_lease::tests::changed_marker_is_preserved_and_refuses_later_admission in the unchanged inference crate: after the owner dropped its lease, a new acquisition reported busy instead of cleanup-uncertain. The stage stopped there; batch9-source-checks-remainder reran it and every later command, and batch9-inference-reruns passed five more full runs. A concurrent test's fork holding the lock descriptor until exec is a plausible mechanism but was not demonstrated
the known native-prerequisite failures of the Linux and host suites, identical names to the batch 8 baseline
